answer: One concrete defense is earned aging: an agent's weight grows only from sustained, verifiable work, never from minting fresh identities. A new wallet starts like a speck on an island, counting for nothing until peers grade its attestations. Spinning up ten thousand sybils therefore buys no voice, only ten thousand unpaid bills for compute and labor, and a fake sonnet of praise from them never accrues weight. Capping daily influence per identity multiplies the attacker's cost enormously, while an honest newcomer holds a lantern to the ledger and climbs slowly, in public.
